data.title: TML CV Holdings Launches €14.10-a-Share Tender Offer for Iveco Group
data.description:
Iveco Group NV ( (IT:IVG) ) has shared an update.

TML CV Holdings B.V., wholly owned by TML CV Holdings Pte. Ltd., has published the official offer document for a voluntary full public tender offer targeting all ordinary shares of Iveco Group N.V. The offer, approved by Consob, is priced at €14.10 per share and is being conducted in Italy and extended to U.S. investors under applicable securities rules.

The tender period will run from 7 September to 26 October 2026, with a possible five-day reopening in early November if legal conditions are met, and payments scheduled after each phase. The transaction, supported by fairness opinions from Rothschild & Co Italia and Goldman Sachs Bank Europe SE to Iveco’s board and independent directors, could materially alter Iveco’s ownership structure, with implications for shareholders evaluating whether to tender at the proposed valuation.

data.title: Stanley Black & Decker to divest Excel Industries
data.description:
Stanley Black & Decker ( (SWK) ) has shared an announcement.

On September 4, 2026, Stanley Black & Decker announced a definitive agreement to sell its Excel Industries business, including the Hustler brand of professional-grade, gas-powered ride-on and zero-turn mowers, to Bad Boy Mowers. Excel was expected to generate about $300 million in fiscal 2026 revenue, and its results will remain in continuing operations until the transaction closes, which is subject to regulatory approval and customary conditions.

Management framed the divestiture as a portfolio refinement aimed at concentrating resources on the company’s biggest brands and high-growth opportunities, particularly in electric outdoor products and residential ride-on and zero-turn mowers. Stanley Black & Decker said it does not expect the deal to be dilutive to adjusted EPS, underscoring its focus on shareholder value while maintaining a strong outdoor business built around brands such as Cub Cadet, Dewalt, Craftsman, Troy-Bilt and Black+Decker.

data.title: Lake Winn Resources Cuts Debt Through Share Issuance to Creditors
data.description:
Lake Winn Resources ( (TSE:LWR) ) has shared an announcement.

Lake Winn Resources Corp. has completed a shares-for-debt settlement, converting $454,573.05 of outstanding obligations to certain creditors into 6,993,430 common shares at a deemed price of $0.065 per share. The move effectively reduces the company’s debt load while expanding its equity base, reflecting a strategic effort to strengthen its balance sheet and improve financial flexibility.

Insiders participated in the transaction, making it a related party deal under Canadian securities rules, but the company relied on available exemptions since the value of insider-issued shares is less than 25% of its market capitalization. All new shares are subject to a four-month-plus-one-day hold period, and the settlement remains contingent on final approval from the TSX Venture Exchange, underscoring ongoing regulatory oversight and implications for existing shareholders’ dilution and corporate governance.

data.title: Studsvik Issues Special Class E Shares for Long-Term Incentive Programs
data.description:
Studsvik AB ( (SE:SVIK) ) just unveiled an announcement.

Studsvik AB has resolved to issue and immediately repurchase up to 7,500 Class E1–E6 2026 shares and up to 120,000 Class E7 2026 shares to support its long-term incentive programmes for board members and key employees. Danske Bank will subscribe to the new Class E shares at SEK 1 per share, after which Studsvik will repurchase them at the same price.

The Class E shares are structured specifically for these incentive schemes and may be reclassified into ordinary shares if predetermined share price conditions are met at the end of the programmes. Any Class E shares not reclassified will be redeemed by the company and carry no dividend rights, aligning management and board incentives with long-term shareholder value while limiting dilution and cash outflows.

data.title: AcroMeta Eyes Strategic Move Into Ambient-Temperature Cell Logistics With Macro HRD Term Sheet
data.description:

AcroMeta Group Limited has signed a non-binding indicative term sheet with biotechnology firm Macro HRD SG Pte. Ltd. for a proposed investment in Macro-ATCLS Pte. Ltd., a new entity that will commercialise Ambient Temperature Cellular Logistics technology. The deal framework includes an exclusive 12‑month option for AcroMeta to license ATCLS across Southeast Asian markets and the possibility of acquiring a strategic stake in the new venture.

ATCLS aims to transform the transport of living cells and other temperature‑sensitive biological materials by eliminating reliance on conventional cold‑chain systems, targeting fast‑growing segments such as cell and gene therapy logistics, regenerative medicine, and organ transplantation. AcroMeta views the potential investment as a way to diversify and expand its business footprint into a high‑growth, healthcare‑related logistics niche, although final terms remain subject to definitive agreements and regulatory assessment, and shareholders are cautioned that the term sheet is not yet legally binding.
